P1.tagline: Lawyer, kinsman and friend of Enfield
P1.bio: Mr. Utterson is a lawyer and the distant kinsman and friend of Mr. Richard Enfield. He is austere, tolerant, and undemonstrative, and is known as the last good influence on downgoing men. On a Sunday walk with Enfield, he was shown a sinister door and heard Enfield's account of a man who trampled a girl and paid with a cheque. Utterson asked whether the cheque drawer lived there, asked the man's name, and asked whether Hyde used a key. He said he already knew the other party's name. He and Enfield agreed never to refer to the matter again. He remains a lawyer and the last good influence on downgoing men.

P2.tagline: Utterson's distant kinsman, man about town
P2.bio: Mr. Richard Enfield is Utterson's distant kinsman and a man about town. He dislikes asking questions and calls it delicacy. On a Sunday walk with Utterson, he pointed his cane at a sinister door and said it was connected with a very odd story. He collared a man who had trampled a girl, forced him to pay a hundred pounds, and spent the night with him in his chambers before taking him to the bank, where the cheque proved genuine. He called the door place Black Mail House, described the door house, named the man as Hyde, and confirmed Hyde still has the key and used it a week ago. He agreed with Utterson never to refer to the matter again.

P3.tagline: Tramples a girl, pays with a cheque
P3.bio: The man in the middle, later named Hyde, is a person of extraordinary appearance who gives a feeling of deformity. He is cool, sneering, and Satan-like. He trampled over a girl's body and left her screaming, then was collared by Enfield and brought back to the group around the child. The doctor turned sick and white with desire to kill him. Threatened with scandal, he was forced to pay a hundred pounds. He led them to the door, unlocked it, and returned with gold and a cheque, offering to stay until the banks opened and cash it himself. They spent the night in Enfield's chambers and went to the bank next day. He still has a key and used it a week ago.
